title: Crash debris analysed as aluminum and barium, matching Brown's Winterhaven proposal

tellings.quote: And where have we seen barium before? Both on the chalkboard at the Bownson labs where Townsend Brown worked and in his Winterhaven proposal. Brown brings up barium to be used in one of his motors for his gravitator discs.

plain: Debris from a crashed object was analysed and found to contain aluminum and barium, and Michels links that barium to the inventor Townsend Brown, whom he presents as a CIA scientist who built disc-shaped craft. Michels says barium showed up both on a chalkboard in the labs where Brown worked and in Brown's Winterhaven proposal of 1953, a plan for his flying discs, in which Brown suggests using barium in one of the motors for his "gravitator discs". Michels makes the connection himself in a documentary about Brown, drawing on the work of Michael Swords, to suggest the crashed material may have something to do with Brown's designs.
